'''Ellis Raymond Ott''' (died December 23, 1981) was an American statistician, consultant and educator.

==Early life==
Ellis Raymond Ott<ref name="shewhart">{{Cite journal |url=https://archive.org/details/sim_industrial-quality-control_1961-08_18_2/page/26/mode/2up |title=Report of the 15th Annual Convention and Exhibit |pages=26–27 |date=August 1961 |journal=Industrial Quality Control |volume=18 |access-date=2025-06-21 |via=[[Archive.org]]}}{{Open access}}</ref> was born in [[Dexter, Kansas]],<ref name="obit">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-central-new-jersey-home-news-profess/174988146/ |title=Professor Ellis R. Ott, 75, Founded RU Statistics Center |date=1981-12-27 |newspaper=The Home News |page=D13 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> to George W. Ott.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-ponca-city-news-father-of-ponca-citi/175005595/ |title=Father of Ponca Citizen Citian Will Be Buried Monday |date=1949-10-02 |newspaper=The Ponca City News |page=5 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-herington-advertiser-returned-to-hom/175007490/ |title=Returned to Homes |date=1947-06-19 |newspaper=The Herington Advertiser |page=4 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> In 1928, he graduated with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] from [[Southwestern College (Kansas)|Southwestern College]] in [[Kansas]]. In 1929, he graduated from the [[University of Kansas]] with a [[Master of Arts]].<ref name="obit"/><ref name="buffalo">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/buffalo-courier-express-new-english-inst/174994059/ |title=New English Instructor |date=1934-09-16 |newspaper=Buffalo Courier-Express |page=12 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> He was a member of [[Gamma Alpha]].<ref name="marriage">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-birmingham-news-ott-tillia-wedding-c/174995978/ |title=Ott-Tillia Wedding Celebrated at Home |date=1932-12-25 |newspaper=The Birmingham News |page=9 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref>

Ott taught at the [[University of Arkansas]] as a mathematics instructor in 1932.<ref name="obit"/> He graduated with a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the [[University of Illinois]] in 1933. He then worked as a graduate assistant at the [[University at Buffalo]].<ref name="buffalo"/><ref name="asq">{{Cite web |url=https://asq.org/about-asq/honorary-members/ott |title=Ellis R. Ott |website=[[American Society for Quality]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1933, Ott became an associate professor of mathematics at the University at Buffalo. He remained there until 1944.<ref name="asq"/><ref name="rutgers">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-central-new-jersey-home-news-dr-ell/174992115/ |title=Dr. Ellis R. Ott Named to Faculty |date=1946-08-23 |newspaper=The Daily Home News |page=16 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> Around 1944 in Buffalo, his interest shifted from college algebra to [[statistical quality control]] as his University at Buffalo colleague [[Martin A. Brumbaugh]] began publishing ''Industrial Quality Control''.<ref name="shewhart"/> In 1946, he joined the National Union Radio Corporation in [[Newark, New Jersey]], as an executive engineer and was in charge at the company of the [[statistical quality control]] of the production of guided missiles.<ref name="asq"/><ref name="shewhart"/> In 1946, he returned to the University at Buffalo. He was a professor of mathematics and assistant dean at the university's Millard Fillmore College until August 1946. At the time, Millard Fillmore College was the University at Buffalo's evening college.<ref name="fellow">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-central-new-jersey-home-news-dr-ell/174991768/ |title=Dr. Ellis R. Ott Elected A Fellow |date=1948-01-23 |newspaper=The Daily Home News |page=5 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref>

Ott then taught at [[Rutgers University]] from 1946 to his retirement in 1972.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="rutgers"/> While there, he developed statistical courses that turned into bachelor and Master of Science degree programs.<ref name="asq"/> In 1948, he started the annual All-Day Conference on Quality Control and Statistics in Industry.<ref name="asq"/><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-star-ledger-dr-ellis-r-ott-25/174993071/ |title=Dr. Ellis R. Ott... |date=1970-08-25 |newspaper=The Star–Ledger |page=15 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> At Rutgers, he taught alongside [[Harold F. Dodge]], [[Martin Wilk]] and [[Horace Andrews]].<ref name="asq"/> He was professor and chairman of the University College Mathematics Department from 1946 to 1959. He was the founding director of the Statistics Center at Rutgers and served as director from 1959 to 1972.<ref name="obit"/> Following his retirement in 1972, he was named professor emeritus.<ref name="asq"/> He traveled to [[India]] in 1952, 1957 and 1962 to teach statistical quality control in association with the [[United Nations]]. He also taught in [[Mexico]] and [[Japan]].<ref name="obit"/><ref name="asq"/> He was a consultant and lecturer on quality control in statistics.<ref name="obit"/> His clients included [[General Electric]], [[Bristol Myers Squibb|Bristol Myers]] and [[Aberdeen Proving Ground]].<ref name="asq"/>

In April 1937, Ott was elected president of the Buffalo section of the [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/buffalo-courier-express-dr-ott-elected/174993556/ |title=Dr. Ott Elected |date=1937-04-27 |newspaper=Buffalo Courier-Express |page=10 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> In June 1942, he was elected president of the Buffalo chapter of the [[American Association of University Professors]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/buffalo-courier-express-educators-elect/174993819/ |title=Educators Elect Officers |date=1943-06-13 |newspaper=Buffalo Courier-Express |page=24 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> He was on the first editorial board of ''Industrial Quality Control'' and served as editor of the practical aids column from 1949 to 1965. The column was later published into a book by Quality Press.<ref name="asq"/> He was a founding member and served as vice president of the [[American Society for Quality|American Society for Quality Control]] from 1956 to 1960.<ref name="asq"/> In January 1950, he succeeded [[Harry G. Romig]] as chairman of the metropolitan section of the American Society for Quality Control.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-central-new-jersey-home-news-elected/174991413/ |title=Elected Chairman of Control Group |date=1950-01-18 |newspaper=The Daily Home News |page=17 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> He co-wrote ''College Algebra'' (1940) with Lewis M. Reagan and Daniel T. Sigley.<ref name="rutgers"/><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/buffalo-courier-express-dr-ellis-r-ott/174993252/ |title=Dr. Ellis R. Ott... |date=1940-04-26 |newspaper=Buffalo Courier-Express |page=10 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-21}}{{Open access}}</ref> He also wrote ''Process Quality Control: Troubleshooting & Interpretation of Data'' (1975). His book ''Process Quality Control'' was based on his experiences consulting. He also contributed articles and papers to professional journals.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="asq"/>

==Personal life==
Ott married Virginia Elinor Tillia, daughter of Henry John Tillia, of [[Des Moines, Iowa]], and [[Birmingham, Alabama]], on December 22, 1932.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="marriage"/> They had three sons, including Steven.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="rutgers"/> In 1946, they lived on Sterling Drive in [[Orange, New Jersey]].<ref name="rutgers"/> Later in life, he lived in [[Piscataway, New Jersey]].<ref name="obit"/>

Ott died on December 23, 1981, aged 75, at his home in [[Marble Falls, Texas]].<ref name="obit"/>

==Awards and legacy==
Ott was elected fellow of the American Society for Quality Control in 1948.<ref name="fellow"/> He was also named an honorary member.<ref name="asq"/> He was also made a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref name="obit"/> He was awarded the [[Shewhart Medal]] in 1960. He was awarded it for his teaching and his leadership in establishing a university graduate program in quality control and applied statistics.<ref name="asq"/><ref name="shewhart"/> He was a recipient of the Grant Award in 1968. In 1968, he won the Brumbaugh Award for his paper ''Analysis of Means (ANOM) – A Graphical Procedure''. He also won the Hoffer Award. He was the namesake of the Ellis R. Ott Award.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="asq"/>

Following his death, colleagues of Ott formed the Ellis R. Ott Foundation in tribute. The foundation's goal is to "honor his memory by advancing the goals to which he devoted decades of tireless effort: Applying statistical quality control to maximize industrial productivity and introducing statistical quality control to a broad spectrum of people."<ref name="asq"/>
